QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_20

question.text: AIF investments are initially recorded at:

answer.text: Cost (fair value at acquisition), then periodically revalued

explanation.text: The Logic: The initial investment can be carried at cost as a prior-transaction or fair-value indicator and may then be revised based on follow-on round pricing. AIF valuation regulations further require Category I and II investments to be periodically valued by an independent valuer at least once every six months, which updates the fund's reported value. The Trap: Zero value ignores the existence of the investment, IPO price applies only to listed securities at a specific event, and target return value is an expectation rather than a recorded basis. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 240, 242, and 243, which describe the IPEV price-of-previous-transaction approach and the at-least-six-month independent valuation requirement for Category I/II AIFs.
